subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow safe read fallback, richer core document extraction, or deferred to broader document/file-input architecture?
rationale: The source-reproducible token-waste problem is real, but the chosen fix changes the core tool boundary and can range from a small warning-only guard to security-sensitive document parsing or provider-native file forwarding.

options.title: Narrow Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a bounded PDF/Office MIME and extension guard in `read` that returns a clear unsupported-document message without parsing Office archives in core.

options.title: Approve Core Extraction
options.body: Define parser dependencies, archive/XML limits, sandbox behavior, and tests before adding native DOCX/PPTX/XLSX extraction to core.

options.title: Defer To File-Input Work
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the broader document extraction and provider-native file-input trackers until maintainers settle that architecture.

recommendation.title: Narrow Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a bounded PDF/Office MIME and extension guard in `read` that returns a clear unsupported-document message without parsing Office archives in core.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Office-path and inbound-media work makes this the strongest routing signal for the read boundary decision.
